html:
Dutch Ceylon was the coastal part of Sri Lanka ruled by the Dutch East India Company from 1640 to 1796. The Dutch came as allies of the hill Kingdom of Kandy against the Portuguese (Portuguese Ceylon). They took Galle in 1640, Colombo in 1656 and Jaffna in 1658, but kept these lands instead of handing them to Kandy.

The colony's main business was cinnamon, peeled by caste workers and sold in Europe at high prices (Dutch Ceylon and cinnamon). It also traded in elephants, pearls and areca nuts. The Dutch built the walled town of Galle Fort, and their Roman Dutch law is still part of Sri Lankan law today. People of Dutch and mixed descent became the Burghers.

In 1796, while the Netherlands was under French control, Britain took the colony. It became British Ceylon in 1802.
